messages.author: eafa26121223327e
messages.subject: cmin = 0 and sparse matrix
parts:
I was wondering if someone would be able to explain in pretty basic terms what the consequences of using cmin=0 are in the "control.inla" option of an spde model with ar1 time series and a normally distributed random variable. I'm running the model using a zero-inflated poisson distribution on count data using a mesh of about 900 vertices. The prior range is 24 km and the max.edge value I've gone with is 12 km on the 'interior' and 16 km on the exterior border area. The plain spatial model runs to completion, although it has huge spatial standard errors. Adding in the ar1 aspect though (10 'groups' each representing a year), results in this repeating error:

"Function: GMFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line 876, Thread :0"
"Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it..."

If I'm understanding the posts on this board correctly, this probably means that some of the estimates in one of my matrices are likely heading into the infinity range at times (?). The recommended solutions I've seen and tried include:

the constr=TRUE option in the spde argument

control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=0.01))

diagonal = 0

diagonal = 0.00001

*Have also tried to adjust the priors on the ar1 and the spde- used both pc priors and normal priors. 

*cmin=0  
     - this option worked without the error described above but also resulted in really large standard errors, so I'm not sure it was very helpful or a good route to take because I can't understand why the standard errors increased so much... 

Should I

1) Interpret this to mean that a temporal model (also tried RW1) is not appropriate or too complicated for the data at hand as these basic temporal models seem to fail?

2) Use cmin=0 and just acknowledge the high SEs? 

3) If not 1 or 2 , are there alternative approaches that others might suggest to approach this challenge? 

Any input or constructive criticism at this point would be greatly appreciated. Please let me know if additional information would be helpful. I'm not knowledgeable enough about the background details of this program to understand 100% what all would be helpful and don't want to make this post overly long. 

Thanks,
KK

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] cmin = 0 and sparse matrix
parts:
On Thu, 2020-01-16 at 06:44 -0800, KK wrote:
> I was wondering if someone would be able to explain in pretty basic
> terms what the consequences of using cmin=0 are in the
> "control.inla" option

the contribution from a datapoint is

log \pi(y_i|eta_i...)

and when doing a Taylor expansion,

log \pi(y_i|eta_i) = A + B * eta_i - 1/2 C eta_i^2 + ...


then 'cmin' defines the minimum value of C, so when its set, it does

C = min(C, cmin)

if 'cmin' is not set, then even a negative value of C could be used.

its a little undefined what is the best option in the case where
'cmin=0' and unset, is different, because it boils down to a log
likelihood that is not log concave, and then what to do.

sometimes, this is caused simply by a to flexible model, so trying to
tighting it up, could help.

H
